First, by the parent-child bijection Ψ ↦ (Ψ ∪ {F(Ψ)}, F(Ψ)), one gets Σ_{r≥0} n_h(r)·r = N(h+1). Second, for a genus-h semigroup Λ with effective generators x_1<...<x_r, if Λ is non-ordinary then for each i the child c_{x_i}(Λ) has exactly (r-i) surviving effective generators x_{i+1},...,x_r, plus one more exactly when x_i is strong; hence e(c_{x_i}(Λ)) = (r-i) + 1_{x_i strong}. For the unique ordinary genus-h semigroup there is one extra effective generator in the child obtained by removing its multiplicity. Summing over all genus-h semigroups gives N(h+2) = 1 + Σ_{r≥0} n_h(r)·r(r-1)/2 + S(h). Therefore the stated lemma is equivalent to the stronger inequality N(h+2) ≥ N(h+1) + N(h) + 1.
